[Nieuhof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Nieuhof "Johan Nieuhof")'s imaginative 1665 map of "Kanton",[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-92) made from secondhand accounts when Europeans were still forbidden from entering the walled city

In October 1646, the [Longwu Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Yujian "Zhu Yujian")'s brother, [Zhu Yuyue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Yuyue "Zhu Yuyue") fled by sea to Guangzhou, the last stronghold of the [Ming empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_dynasty "Ming dynasty"). On December 11, he declared himself the Shaowu Emperor, borrowing his imperial regalia from local theater troupes.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985737-93) He led a successful offense against his cousin [Zhu Youlang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Youlang "Zhu Youlang") but was deposed and executed on January 20, 1647, when the Ming turncoat Li Chengdong ([李](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%9D%8E "wikt:李")[成](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%88%90 "wikt:成")[棟](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%A3%9F "wikt:棟")) sacked the city on behalf of the [Qing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_dynasty "Qing dynasty").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985738-94)

In May 1648, Li Chengdong rebelled against the Qing and declared his allegiance to the [Southern Ming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Ming "Southern Ming"), making Guangzhou a base for the Ming loyalist resurgence in southern China.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985764%E2%80%93767-95) On 24 November 1650, after a prolonged siege during the [Qing conquest of southern China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transition_from_Ming_to_Qing "Transition from Ming to Qing"), [Shang Kexi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shang_Kexi "Shang Kexi")'s forces captured Guangzhou and launched a large-scale massacre of Ming loyalists and civilians, killing up to 70,000 people.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985767%E2%80%93768-96)

The Qing became somewhat more receptive to foreign trade after gaining control of [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Tungning "Kingdom of Tungning") in 1683.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerdue2009-97) The [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire") from [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Macau "Colonial Macau") and [Spaniards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire") from [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Philippines "Spanish Philippines") returned, as did private Muslim, [Armenian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians "Armenians"), and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_England "Kingdom of England") traders.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) From 1699 to 1714, the [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV's_East_India_Company "Louis XIV's East India Company") and [British East India Companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company "East India Company") sent a ship or two each year;[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) the [Austrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Empire "Austrian Empire")[Ostend General India Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostend_Company "Ostend Company") arrived in 1717,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEButel1997197-99) the [Dutch East India Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_India_Company "Dutch East India Company") in 1729,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-100) the [Danish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway-Denmark "Norway-Denmark")[Asiatic Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_Asiatic_Company "Danish Asiatic Company") in 1731, and the [Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sweden "Kingdom of Sweden")[East India Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_East_India_Company "Swedish East India Company") the next year.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) These were joined by the occasional [Prussian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Prussia "Kingdom of Prussia") or [Trieste Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trieste_Company "Trieste Company") vessel. The first independent American ship arrived in 1784, and the first [colonial Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Australia "Colonial Australia") one in 1788.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] By that time, Guangzhou was one of the world's greatest ports, organized under the [Canton System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_System "Canton System").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKjellberg197599-101) The main exports were [tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_tea "History of tea") and [porcelain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_porcelain "Chinese porcelain").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) As a meeting place of merchants from all over the world, Guangzhou became a major contributor to the rise of the modern global economy.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-102) Guangzhou is the site of the [Thirteen Factories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Factories "Thirteen Factories"), which were the only legal place to conduct foreign trade with China from 1757 to 1842.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-103):xviii

In the 19th century, most of the city's buildings were still only one or two stories. However, there were notable exceptions such as the [Flower Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower_Pagoda "Flower Pagoda") of the [Temple of the Six Banyan Trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_of_the_Six_Banyan_Trees "Temple of the Six Banyan Trees"), and the guard tower known as the [Five-Story Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhenhai_Tower_(Guangzhou) "Zhenhai Tower (Guangzhou)"). The subsequently urbanized northern hills were bare and covered with traditional graves. The brick city walls were about 6 miles (10 km) in circumference, 25 feet (8 m) high, and 20 feet (6 m) wide. Its eight main gates and two water gates all held guards during the day and were closed at night. The wall rose to incorporate a hill on its northern side and was surrounded on the other three by a moat which, along with the canals, functioned as the city's sewer, emptied daily by the river's tides. A partition wall with four gates divided the northern "old town" from the southern "new town" closer to the river; the suburb of [Xiguan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiguan "Xiguan") (Saikwan; "West Gate") stretched beyond and the boats of fishers, traders, and [Tanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanka_people "Tanka people") ("boat people") almost entirely concealed the riverbank for about 4 miles (6 km). It was common for homes to have a storefront facing the street and to treat their [courtyards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_courtyard_house "Chinese courtyard house") as a kind of warehouse.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''EB''187837-42) The city was part of a network of signal towers so effective that messages could be relayed to [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing")—about 1,200 miles (1,931 km) away—in less than 24 hours.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKjellberg197595-104)

The Canton System was maintained until the outbreak of the [First Opium War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Opium_War "First Opium War") in 1839. Following a series of battles in the [Pearl River Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River_Delta "Pearl River Delta"), the British [captured Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Canton_(March_1841) "Battle of Canton (March 1841)") on March 18, 1841.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''Bulletins_&c.''1841357-105) The [Second Battle of Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Canton_(May_1841) "Battle of Canton (May 1841)") was fought two months later.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMacPherson1842312_&_315-106) Following the Qing's 1842 [treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Nanking "Treaty of Nanking") with [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland"), Guangzhou lost its privileged trade status as more and more [treaty ports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_port "Treaty port") were opened to more and more countries, usually including extraterritorial enclaves. Amid the decline of Qing prestige and the chaos of the [Red Turban Rebellion (1854–1856)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Turban_Rebellion_(1854%E2%80%931856) "Red Turban Rebellion (1854–1856)"), the [Punti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punti "Punti") and [Hakka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hakka "Hakka") waged [a series of clan wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punti-Hakka_Clan_Wars "Punti-Hakka Clan Wars") from 1855 to 1867 in which one million people died. The foreign trade facilities were destroyed by local Chinese in the [Arrow War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Opium_War "Second Opium War") (1856–1858). The international community relocated to the outskirts and most international trade moved through [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-107)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-108)

The concession for the [Guangzhou–Hankou railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou%E2%80%93Hankou_railway "Guangzhou–Hankou railway") was awarded to the [American China Development Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_China_Development_Company "American China Development Company") in 1898. It completed [its branch line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou%E2%80%93Sanshui_Railway "Guangzhou–Sanshui Railway") west to [Foshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foshan "Foshan") and [Sanshui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanshui "Sanshui") before being engulfed in a diplomatic crisis after a Belgian consortium bought a controlling interest and the Qing subsequently canceled its concession. [J. P. Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Morgan "J. P. Morgan") was awarded millions in damages[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-109) and the line to [Wuchang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuchang_District "Wuchang District") was not completed until 1936[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-110) and the completion of a unified [Beijing–Guangzhou railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing%E2%80%93Guangzhou_railway "Beijing–Guangzhou railway") waited until the completion of [Wuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan")'s [Yangtze River Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan_Yangtze_River_Bridge "Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge") in 1957.

### Modern China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Modern China")]

#### Revolutions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Revolutions")]

During the late Qing dynasty, Guangzhou was the site of revolutionary attempts such as the [Uprisings of 1895](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Guangzhou_Uprising "First Guangzhou Uprising") and [1911](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Guangzhou_Uprising#History "Second Guangzhou Uprising") that were the predecessors of the successful [1911 Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1911_Revolution "1911 Revolution"), which overthrew the Qing dynasty. The 72 revolutionaries whose bodies were found after the latter uprising are honored as the city's 72 [Martyrs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martyrdom_in_Chinese_culture "Martyrdom in Chinese culture") at the [Huanghuagang Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huanghuagang_Park?action=edit&redlink=1 "Huanghuagang Park (page does not exist)")[[zh](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%BB%84%E8%8A%B1%E5%B2%97%E5%85%AC%E5%9B%AD "zh:黄花岗公园")] (_Yellow Flower Mound Park_).

#### Republic of China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Republic of China")]

After the assassination of [Song Jiaoren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_Jiaoren "Song Jiaoren") and [Yuan Shikai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_Shikai "Yuan Shikai")'s attempts to remove the [Nationalist Party of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_Party_of_China "Nationalist Party of China") from power, the leader of Guangdong [Hu Hanmin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Hanmin "Hu Hanmin") joined the 1913 [Second Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Revolution_(China) "Second Revolution (China)") against him[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-111) but was forced to flee to [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan") with [Sun Yat-sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-sen "Sun Yat-sen") after its failure. The city came under national spotlight again in 1917, when Prime Minister [Duan Qirui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duan_Qirui "Duan Qirui")'s abrogation of the constitution triggered the [Constitutional Protection Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Protection_Movement "Constitutional Protection Movement"). [Sun Yat-sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-sen "Sun Yat-sen") came to head the [Guangzhou Military Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Protection_Junta "Constitutional Protection Junta") supported by the members of the dissolved parliament and the Southwestern warlords. The Guangzhou government fell apart as the warlords withdrew their support. Sun fled to [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_International_Settlement "Shanghai International Settlement") in November 1918 until the Guangdong warlord [Chen Jiongming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Jiongming "Chen Jiongming") restored him in October 1920 during the [Yuegui Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuegui_Wars "Yuegui Wars").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeck2007-112) On June 16, 1922, Sun was ousted in a coup and fled on the warship _[Yongfeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS\_Zhongshan "SS Zhongshan")_ after Chen sided with the [Zhili clique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhili_clique "Zhili clique")'s [Beijing government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beiyang_government "Beiyang government"). In the following months Sun mounted a counterattack into Guangdong by rallying supporters from Yunnan and Guangxi, and in January established [a government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_the_Republic_of_China_in_Guangzhou "Government of the Republic of China in Guangzhou") in the city for the third time.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

From 1923 to 1926, Sun Yat-sen and the [Kuomintang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuomintang "Kuomintang") (KMT) [used the city as a base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_and_Navy_Marshal_stronghold_of_the_Republic_of_China "Army and Navy Marshal stronghold of the Republic of China") to prosecute a renewed revolution in China by conquering the warlords in the north. Although Sun was previously dependent on opportunistic warlords who hosted him in the city, with the leadership of [Chiang Kai-shek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek "Chiang Kai-shek"), the KMT developed its own military power to serve its ambition. The Canton years saw the evolution of the KMT into a revolutionary movement with a strong military focus and ideological commitment, setting the tone of the KMT rule of China beyond 1927.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1924, the KMT made the momentous decision to ally with the Communist Party and the USSR. With Soviet help, KMT reorganized itself along the Leninist line and adopted a pro-labor and pro-peasant stance. The [KMT–CCP cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_United_Front "First United Front") was confirmed in the [1st National Congress of the KMT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_National_Congress_of_the_Kuomintang "1st National Congress of the Kuomintang") and the communists were instructed to join the KMT. The allied government set up the [Peasant Movement Training Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peasant_Movement_Training_Institute "Peasant Movement Training Institute") in the city, of which [Mao Zedong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong") was a director for one term. Sun and his military commander Chiang used [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USSR "USSR") funds and weapons to build an armed force staffed by communist commissars, training its cadres in the [Whampoa Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whampoa_Military_Academy "Whampoa Military Academy").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeck2007-112) In August, the fledgling army suppressed the [Canton Merchants' Corps Uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_Merchants'_Corps_Uprising "Canton Merchants' Corps Uprising"). The next year the anti-imperialist [May Thirtieth Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_Thirtieth_Movement "May Thirtieth Movement") swept the country, and the KMT government called for strikes in Canton and Hong Kong. The tensions of the massive strikes and protests led to the [Shakee Massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakee_Massacre "Shakee Massacre").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

After the death of Sun Yat-sen in 1925 the mood was changing in the party toward the communists. In August the left-wing KMT leader [Liao Zhongkai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_Zhongkai "Liao Zhongkai") was assassinated and the right-wing leader [Hu Hanmin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Hanmin "Hu Hanmin"), the suspected mastermind, was exiled to the Soviet Union, leaving the pro-communist [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei") in charge. Opposing communist encroachment, the right-wing [Western Hills Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hills_Group "Western Hills Group") vowed to expel the communists from the KMT. The [Canton Coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_Coup "Canton Coup") on March 20, 1926, saw Chiang solidify his control over the [Nationalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KMT "KMT") and [their army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Revolutionary_Army "National Revolutionary Army") against [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei"), the party's left wing, its [Communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") allies, and its [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USSR "USSR") advisors.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-113)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-AhXiang1998-114) By May, he had ended civilian control of the military[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-AhXiang1998-114) and begun his [Northern Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Expedition_(1926%E2%80%931927) "Northern Expedition (1926–1927)") against the [warlords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warlord_Era "Warlord Era") of the north. Its success led to the split of the KMT between Wuhan and Nanking and the purge of the communists in the [April 12 Incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_12_Incident "April 12 Incident"). Immediately afterwards Canton joined the purge under the auspice of [Li Jishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jishen "Li Jishen"), resulting in the arrest of communists and the suspension of left wing KMT apparatuses and labor groups. Later in 1927 when [Zhang Fakui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Fakui "Zhang Fakui"), a general supportive of the Wuhan faction, seized Canton and installed [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei")'s faction in the city, the communists saw an opening and launched the [Guangzhou Uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou_Uprising "Guangzhou Uprising"). Prominent communist military leaders [Ye Ting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_Ting "Ye Ting") and [Ye Jianying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_Jianying "Ye Jianying") led the failed defense of the city. Soon, control of the city reverted to [Li Jishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jishen "Li Jishen").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Li Jishen was deposed during a war between Chiang and the [New Guangxi clique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Guangxi_clique "New Guangxi clique"). By 1929, [Chen Jitang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Jitang "Chen Jitang") had established himself as the powerholder of Guangdong. In 1931 he threw his weight behind the anti-Chiang schism by hosting a separate Nationalist government in Guangzhou.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-115) The opposition to Chiang included KMT leaders like [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei"), [Sun Fo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Fo "Sun Fo") and others from diverse factions. The peace negotiations amid the armed standoff led to the [4th National Congress of Kuomintang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_National_Congress_of_Kuomintang "4th National Congress of Kuomintang") being held separately by three factions in Nanjing, Shanghai, and Canton. Resigning all his posts, Chiang pulled off a political compromise that reunited all factions. While the intraparty division was resolved, Chen kept his power until he was defeated by Chiang in 1936. During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the [Canton Operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_Operation "Canton Operation") subjected the city to [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan") occupation by the end of December 1938.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### People's Republic of China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: People's Republic of China")]

Amid the closing months before total Communist victory, Guangzhou briefly served as the capital of the Republican government. Guangzhou was captured on October 14, 1949. Amid a massive exodus to [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Macau "Colonial Macau"), defeated Nationalist forces blew up the [Haizhu Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haizhu_Bridge "Haizhu Bridge") across the Pearl River in retreat. The Cultural Revolution had a large effect on the city, with many of its temples, churches and other monuments destroyed during this chaotic period.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") initiated building projects including new housing on the banks of the Pearl River to adjust the city's [boat people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanka_people "Tanka people") to life on land. Since the 1980s, the city's close proximity to [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and its ties to [overseas Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Chinese "Overseas Chinese") made it one of the first beneficiaries of China's [opening up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_up_policy "Opening up policy") under [Deng Xiaoping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping"). British pop duo [Wham!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wham! "Wham!") performed in the city in April 1985, their second China date of [the Big Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Big_Tour "The Big Tour") after Beijing, becoming the first Western pop act to perform in China.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-116) Beneficial tax reforms in the 1990s also helped the city's industrialization and economic development.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The municipality was expanded in the year 2000, with [Huadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huadu_District "Huadu District") and [Panyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panyu_District "Panyu District") joining the city as [urban districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_(China) "District (China)") and [Conghua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conghua "Conghua") and [Zengcheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zengcheng "Zengcheng") as more rural [counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(China) "County (China)"). The former districts of [Dongshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dongshan_District,_Guangzhou "Dongshan District, Guangzhou") and [Fangcun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fangcun_District "Fangcun District") were abolished in 2005, merged into [Yuexiu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuexiu_District "Yuexiu District") and [Liwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liwan_District "Liwan District") respectively. The city acquired [Nansha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nansha,_Guangzhou "Nansha, Guangzhou") and [Luogang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luogang_District "Luogang District"). The former was carved out of [Panyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panyu_District "Panyu District"), the latter from parts of [Baiyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baiyun_District,_Guangzhou "Baiyun District, Guangzhou"), [Tianhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianhe_District "Tianhe District"), [Zengcheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zengcheng "Zengcheng"), and an exclave within [Huangpu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_District,_Guangzhou "Huangpu District, Guangzhou"). The [National People's Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_People's_Congress "National People's Congress") approved a development plan for the [Pearl River Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River_Delta "Pearl River Delta") in January 2009; on March 19 of the same year, the Guangzhou and [Foshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foshan "Foshan") municipal governments agreed to establish a framework to merge the two cities.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-117) In 2014, [Luogang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luogang_District "Luogang District") merged into [Huangpu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_District,_Guangzhou "Huangpu District, Guangzhou") and both [Conghua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conghua_District "Conghua District") and [Zengcheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zengcheng_District "Zengcheng District") counties were upgraded to districts.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 16 June 2022, an [EF2 tornado struck the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornadoes_of_2022#June_16_(China) "Tornadoes of 2022"), causing major power outages and knocking out power to the city's subway lines.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-118)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-119)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-120)

**Guangzhou**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-7) also known as **Canton**,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-8) is the [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city "Capital city") and largest city of [Guangdong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangdong "Guangdong") in [southern China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_China "South China").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-9) Located on the [Pearl River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River "Pearl River"), about 120 kilometres (75 mi) northwest of [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and 145 kilometres (90 mi) north of [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macau "Macau"), Guangzhou has a history of over 2,200 years and was a major terminus of the [Silk Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Road "Silk Road").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-10)

The [port of Guangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Guangzhou "Port of Guangzhou") serves as a transportation hub. Guangzhou is also one of China's three largest cities.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-11) For a long time, it was the only Chinese port accessible to the Europeans. Guangzhou was captured by the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") during the [First Opium War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Opium_War "First Opium War") and no longer enjoyed a monopoly after the war. Consequently, it lost trade to other ports such as Hong Kong and [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai"), but continued to serve as a major [entrepôt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrep%C3%B4t "Entrepôt") at China.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-12)

Guangzhou is at the center of the [Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macau Greater Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangdong%E2%80%93Hong_Kong%E2%80%93Macau_Greater_Bay_Area "Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macau Greater Bay Area"), the most populous built-up metropolitan region in the world. The area extends into neighboring cities such as [Foshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foshan "Foshan"), [Dongguan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dongguan "Dongguan"), [Zhongshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhongshan "Zhongshan"), [Shenzhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhen "Shenzhen"), parts of [Jiangmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangmen "Jiangmen") and [Huizhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huizhou "Huizhou"), as well as [Zhuhai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhuhai "Zhuhai") and Macau, forming an [urban agglomeration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area "Urban area") of about 70 million residents.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-13) It is also part of the [Pearl River Delta Economic Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River_Delta_Economic_Zone "Pearl River Delta Economic Zone"). Administratively, the city holds [subprovincial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-provincial_division "Sub-provincial division") status[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-14) and is one of China's nine [National Central Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Central_City "National Central City").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-15) In the late 1990s and early 2000s, nationals of [sub-Saharan Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_Africa "Sub-Saharan Africa") who had initially settled in the Middle East and Southeast Asia moved in unprecedented numbers to Guangzhou in response to the [1997/98 Asian financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Asian_financial_crisis "1997 Asian financial crisis").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-16) The [domestic migrant population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migration_in_China "Migration in China") from other [provinces of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_China "Provinces of China") in Guangzhou was 40% of the city's total population in 2008. Guangzhou has one of the most expensive real estate markets in China.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-cnd-17) As of the 2020 census, the registered population of the city's expansive administrative area was 18,676,605 individuals (up 47 percent from the previous census in 2010), of whom 16,492,590 lived in 9 urban districts (all but [Conghua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conghua_District "Conghua District") and [Zengcheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zengcheng_District "Zengcheng District")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-citypopulation.de-2) Due to worldwide travel restrictions at the beginning of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), [Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou_Baiyun_International_Airport "Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport"), the major airport of Guangzhou, briefly became the [world's busiest airport by passenger traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_busiest_airports_by_passenger_traffic "List of busiest airports by passenger traffic") in 2020.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-18) Guangzhou is the fifth most populous city by urban resident population in China after Shanghai, [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), [Shenzhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhen "Shenzhen") and [Chongqing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chongqing "Chongqing").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-19)

In modern commerce, Guangzhou is best known for its annual [Canton Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_Fair "Canton Fair"), the oldest and largest [trade fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_fair "Trade fair") in China.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-20) For three consecutive years (2013–2015), Forbes ranked Guangzhou as the best commercial city in mainland China.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-21) Guangzhou is highly ranked as an [Alpha (global first-tier)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network "Globalization and World Cities Research Network") city together with [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") and [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-22) It is a major [Asia-Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia-Pacific "Asia-Pacific") finance hub, ranking 21st globally in the 2020 [Global Financial Centres Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Financial_Centres_Index "Global Financial Centres Index").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-GFCI-23) Guangzhou also has [the fifth largest number of skyscrapers in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_with_the_most_skyscrapers "List of cities with the most skyscrapers"). As an important international city, Guangzhou has hosted numerous international and national sporting events, the most notable being the [2010 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Asian_Games "2010 Asian Games"), the [2010 Asian Para Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Asian_Para_Games "2010 Asian Para Games"), and the [2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_FIBA_Basketball_World_Cup "2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup"). The city hosts 65 [foreign representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_in_China#Guangzhou "List of diplomatic missions in China"), making it the major city hosting the third most foreign representatives in China, after Beijing and Shanghai.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-GC-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-CE-25) As of 2020, Guangzhou ranked 10th in the world and 5th in China—after Beijing, Shanghai, Hong Kong and Shenzhen—for the number of billionaire residents by the [Hurun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Hoogewerf "Rupert Hoogewerf") Global Rich List.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-SS-26) Guangzhou is one of the nation's leading hubs for academia and academic research, [ranking 6th globally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_scientific_output "List of cities by scientific output"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-l2-27) and is home to numerous [Double First-Class Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_First-Class_Construction "Double First-Class Construction"), including [Sun Yat-sen University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-sen_University "Sun Yat-sen University") and [SCUT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_China_University_of_Technology "South China University of Technology").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-30)

## Toponymy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Toponymy")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Wuxian_Xiadong.jpg/250px-Wuxian_Xiadong.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wuxian_Xiadong.jpg)

Portrait of the [Grotto of the Five Immortals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grotto_of_the_Five_Immortals "Grotto of the Five Immortals"), the [Taoist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taoist "Taoist") temple around the five stones which gave Guangzhou its nickname "The City of Rams"

_Guǎngzhōu_ is the official [romanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Chinese "Romanization of Chinese") of the Chinese name 广州 in [Mandarin Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandarin_Chinese "Mandarin Chinese"). The name of the city is taken from the ancient [Guǎng Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C7%8Eng_Prefecture "Guǎng Prefecture") after it had become the prefecture's seat of government. The [character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_character "Chinese character")[廣](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%BB%A3#Traditional_Chinese "wikt:廣") or [广](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%B9%BF#Simplified_Chinese "wikt:广") means 'broad' or 'expansive'.

Before acquiring its current name, the town was known as Panyu (Punyü; [番禺](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%95%AA%E7%A6%BA#Traditional_Chinese "wikt:番禺")), a name still borne by [one of Guangzhou's districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panyu_District "Panyu District") not far from the main city. The origin of the name is still uncertain, with 11 various explanations being offered,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-31) including that it may have referred to two local mountains.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-32)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-33) The city has also sometimes been known as Guangzhou Fu or Guangfu after its status as the capital of a [prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fu_(administrative_division) "Fu (administrative division)"). From this latter name, Guangzhou was known to medieval Persians such as [Al-Masudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Masudi "Al-Masudi") and [Ibn Khordadbeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibn_Khordadbeh "Ibn Khordadbeh")[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-34) as Khanfu (خانفو).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-35) Under the [Southern Han](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Han "Southern Han"), the city was renamed Xingwang Fu (興王府).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-37)

The [Chinese abbreviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_abbreviation "Chinese abbreviation") for Guangzhou is [穗](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%A9%97#Chinese "wikt:穗"), pronounced _Seoi 6_ in Cantonese and _Suì_ in Mandarin—although the abbreviation on car license plates, as with the rest of the province, is [粤](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%B2%A4#Simplified_Chinese "wikt:粤")), after its nickname "City of Rice" ([穗城](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%A9%97%E5%9F%8E#Chinese "wikt:穗城")). The city has long borne the nickname City of Rams ([羊城](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%BE%8A%E5%9F%8E#Chinese "wikt:羊城")) or City of the Five Rams ([五羊城](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E4%BA%94%E7%BE%8A%E5%9F%8E#Chinese "wikt:五羊城")) from the five stones at the old [Temple of the Five Immortals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_of_the_Five_Immortals_(Guangzhou) "Temple of the Five Immortals (Guangzhou)") said to have been the sheep or goats ridden by the [Taoist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taoism "Taoism")[culture heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_hero "Culture hero") credited with introducing [rice cultivation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_cultivation "Rice cultivation") to the area around the time of the city's foundation.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-38) The former name "City of the [Immortals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taoist_Immortal "Taoist Immortal")" ([仙城](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E4%BB%99%E5%9F%8E#Chinese "wikt:仙城")/五仙城) came from the same story. The more recent City of Flowers ([花城](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E8%8A%B1%E5%9F%8E#Chinese "wikt:花城")) is usually taken as a simple reference to the area's fine greenery.

The English name "Canton" derived from [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language")_Cidade de Cantão_,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-39) a blend of [dialectal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialects_of_Chinese "Dialects of Chinese") pronunciations of "Guangdong"[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-41) (e.g., [Cantonese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonese "Cantonese")_Gwong2-dung1_). Although it originally and chiefly applied to the walled city, it was occasionally conflated with Guangdong by some authors. It was adopted as the [Postal Map Romanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postal_Map_Romanization "Postal Map Romanization") of Guangzhou, and remained the official name until its [name change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin") to "Guangzhou". As an adjective, it is still used in describing the [people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonese_people "Cantonese people"), [language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonese_language "Cantonese language"), [cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonese_cuisine "Cantonese cuisine") and [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonese_culture "Cantonese culture") of Guangzhou and the surrounding Liangguang region. The 19th-century name was "Kwang-chow foo".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''EB''187837-42)

For a chronological guide, see [Timeline of Guangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Guangzhou "Timeline of Guangzhou").

### Prehistory

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Prehistory")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Si_l%C3%BC_yu_yi.JPG/250px-Si_l%C3%BC_yu_yi.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Si_l%C3%BC_yu_yi.JPG)

The [jade burial suit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jade_burial_suit "Jade burial suit") of [Zhao Mo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Mo "Zhao Mo") in Guangzhou's [Nanyue King Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanyue_King_Museum "Nanyue King Museum")

Prior to the [Han conquest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_conquest_of_Nanyue "Han conquest of Nanyue"), the area of modern Guangzhou was inhabited by indigenous, non-Chinese tribes known collectively as the [Baiyue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baiyue "Baiyue").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-43)

A settlement now known as Nanwucheng was present in the area by 1100 BC.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-45) Some traditional Chinese histories placed Nanwucheng's founding during the reign of [King Nan of Zhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Nan_of_Zhou "King Nan of Zhou"),[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-anatomy-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-acc-47)[emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Zhou_emperors "List of Zhou emperors") of [Zhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_dynasty "Zhou dynasty") from 314 to 256 BC. It was said to have consisted of little more than a stockade of bamboo and mud.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-anatomy-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-acc-47)

### Nanyue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Nanyue")]

Guangzhou, then known as **Panyu**, was founded on the eastern bank of the [Pearl River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River_(China) "Pearl River (China)") in 214 BC.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''EB''187837-42) Ships commanded by [tradespersons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tradesperson "Tradesperson") arrived on the South China coast in the late [antiquity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiquities "Antiquities"). Surviving records from the [Tang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty "Tang dynasty") confirm, that the residents of Panyu observed a range of trade missions. Records on foreign trade ships reach upon til the late 20th century.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-48)

Panyu was the seat of [Qin Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qin_Empire "Qin Empire")'s [Nanhai Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanhai_Commandery "Nanhai Commandery"), and served as a base for the [first invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qin_conquest_of_Guangdong "Qin conquest of Guangdong") of the [Baiyue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baiyue "Baiyue") lands in southern China. Legendary accounts claimed that the soldiers at Panyu were so vigilant that they did not remove their armor for three years.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-49) Upon the [fall of the Qin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Qin "Fall of the Qin"), General [Zhao Tuo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Tuo "Zhao Tuo") established the kingdom of [Nanyue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanyue "Nanyue") and made Panyu its capital in 204 BC. It remained independent throughout the [Chu-Han Contention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu-Han_Contention "Chu-Han Contention"), although Zhao negotiated recognition of his independence in exchange for his nominal submission to the [Han](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_dynasty "Han dynasty") in 196 BC.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-50) Archeological evidence shows that Panyu was an expansive commercial center: in addition to items from central China, archeologists have found remains originating from [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia"), India, and even Africa.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-51) Zhao Tuo was succeeded by [Zhao Mo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Mo "Zhao Mo") and then Zhao Yingqi. Upon [Zhao Yingqi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Yingqi "Zhao Yingqi")'s death in 115 BC, his younger son [Zhao Xing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Xing "Zhao Xing") was named as his successor in violation of Chinese [primogeniture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primogeniture "Primogeniture"). By 113 BC, his [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_people "Han people") mother, the Empress Dowager Jiu ([樛](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%A8%9B "wikt:樛")) had prevailed upon him to submit Nanyue as a formal part of the Han Empire. The native [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_councillor "Grand councillor")[Lü Jia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%BC_Jia_(Nanyue) "Lü Jia (Nanyue)") launched a coup, killing Han ambassadors along with the king, his mother, and their supporters.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEY%C3%BC1987453-52) A successful ambush then annihilated a Han force which had been sent to arrest him. [Emperor Wu of Han](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Wu_of_Han "Emperor Wu of Han") took offense and launched [a massive riverine and seaborne war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han%E2%80%93Nanyue_War "Han–Nanyue War"): six armies under [Lu Bode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Bode "Lu Bode") and Yang Pu[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-53) took Panyu and annexed Nanyue by the end of 111 BC.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEY%C3%BC1987453-52)

### Imperial China

Incorporated into the [Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Han_dynasty "Western Han dynasty"), Panyu became a provincial capital. In AD 226, it became the seat of Guang [Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_(country_subdivision) "Zhou (country subdivision)"), which gave it its modern name. The _[Old Book of Tang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old\_Book\_of\_Tang "Old Book of Tang")_ described Guangzhou as an important port in southern China.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-54) Direct routes connected the Middle East and China, as shown in the records of a Chinese prisoner returning home from Iraq twelve years after his capture at [Talas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Talas "Battle of Talas").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-55) Relations were often strained: while China was undergoing the [An Lushan Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_Lushan_Rebellion "An Lushan Rebellion"), Arab and Persian pirates[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-IH-56)[sacked the city on 30 October 758](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sack_of_Guangzhou_(758) "Sack of Guangzhou (758)")[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-bret-57)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-welsh-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-need-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-sima-60) and in revenge thousands of Arabs and Persians were killed by Chinese rebels in the [Yangzhou massacre (760)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangzhou_massacre_(760) "Yangzhou massacre (760)"). In the [Guangzhou massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou_massacre "Guangzhou massacre") about 200,000 Arab, Persian and other foreigners were killed by Chinese rebel [Huang Chao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huang_Chao "Huang Chao") in 878, along with the city's [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews"), [Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians "Christians"),[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-frenchy-61)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-kaifung-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-gibberish-63) and [Parsis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parsi "Parsi").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-sirafi-64)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-guy-65) The port was closed for fifty years after its destruction.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-IH-56)

Amid the [Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_Dynasties_and_Ten_Kingdoms "Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms") that followed the collapse of the [Tang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty "Tang dynasty"), the [Later Liang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Later_Liang_(Five_Dynasties) "Later Liang (Five Dynasties)") governor [Liu Yan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Yan_(emperor) "Liu Yan (emperor)") used his base at Panyu to establish a "Great Yue" or "[Southern Han](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Han "Southern Han")" empire, which lasted from 917 to 971. The region enjoyed considerable cultural and economic success in this period. From the 10th to 12th century, there are records that the large foreign communities were not exclusively men, but included "[Persian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_people "Persian people") females".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-67) According to [Odoric of Pordenone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odoric_of_Pordenone "Odoric of Pordenone"), Guangzhou was as large as three Venices in terms of area, and rivaled all of Italy in the amount of crafts produced. He also noted the large amount of ginger available as well as large geese and snakes.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEYule2002121-68) Guangzhou was visited by the [Moroccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moroccan_people "Moroccan people") traveler [Ibn Battuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibn_Battuta "Ibn Battuta") during his journey around the world in the 14th century.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDunn1986259-69) He detailed the process by which the Chinese constructed their large ships in the port's shipyards.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-70)

Shortly after the [Hongwu Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hongwu_Emperor "Hongwu Emperor")'s declaration of the [Ming dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_dynasty "Ming dynasty"), he reversed his earlier support of [foreign trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_trade "Foreign trade") and imposed the first of a series of [sea bans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haijin "Haijin").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVon_Glahn199690-71) These banned private foreign trade upon penalty of death for the merchant and exile for his family and neighbors.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTELi20103-72) Previous maritime intendancies of Guangzhou, [Quanzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quanzhou "Quanzhou"), and [Ningbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ningbo "Ningbo") were closed in 1384[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVon_Glahn1996116-73) and legal trade became limited to the [tribute delegations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Chinese_tributary_system "Imperial Chinese tributary system") sent to or by official representatives of foreign governments.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVon_Glahn199691-74)

Following the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire")[conquest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capture_of_Malacca_(1511) "Capture of Malacca (1511)") of the [Melaka Sultanate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melaka_Sultanate "Melaka Sultanate"), [Rafael Perestrello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Perestrello "Rafael Perestrello") traveled to Guangzhou as a passenger on a native [junk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junk_(ship) "Junk (ship)") in 1516.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''Knight's''1841135-75) His report induced [Fernão Pires de Andrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fern%C3%A3o_Pires_de_Andrade "Fernão Pires de Andrade") to sail to the city with eight ships the next piracy,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDutra_&_al.1995426-80) and fortifying the island of [Tamão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tam%C3%A3o "Tamão").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWills1998337%E2%80%93338-81)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTECortesao1944xxxvii-82) Rumors even circulated that Portuguese were eating the children.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-sjay-83)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWills_&_al.201028-84) The Guangzhou administration was Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Xicaowan "Battle of Xicaowan"); held a [diplomatic mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A9_Pires "Tomé Pires") hostage in a failed attempt to vassal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Chinese_tributary_system "Imperial Chinese tributary system");[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWills1998340-87) and, after placing them in [cangues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cangue "Cangue") and keeping them for most of a year, ultimately executed 23 by [lingchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingchi "Lingchi").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTECortesao1944xliv%E2%80%93v-88) With the help of local pirates,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-sjay-83) the "[Folangji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folangji "Folangji")" then carried out smuggling at [Macao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Macao "Portuguese Macao"), [Lampacau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lampacau "Lampacau"), and St John's Island (now [Shangchuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shangchuan_Island "Shangchuan Island")),[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDouglas200611-79) until [Leonel de Sousa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonel_de_Sousa "Leonel de Sousa") legalized their trade with bribes to Admiral Wang Bo ([汪](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%B1%AA "wikt:汪")[柏](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%9F%8F "wikt:柏")) and the [1554 Luso-Chinese Accord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luso-Chinese_agreement_(1554) "Luso-Chinese agreement (1554)"). The Portuguese undertook not to raise fortifications and to pay customs dues;[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWills1998343-89) three years later, after providing the Chinese with assistance suppressing their former pirate allies,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWills1998343%E2%80%93344-90) the Portuguese were permitted to warehouse their goods at [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Macau "Colonial Macau") instead of Guangzhou itself.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-heyporter-91)

[Nieuhof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Nieuhof "Johan Nieuhof")'s imaginative 1665 map of "Kanton",[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-92) made from secondhand accounts when Europeans were still forbidden from entering the walled city

In October 1646, the [Longwu Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Yujian "Zhu Yujian")'s brother, [Zhu Yuyue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Yuyue "Zhu Yuyue") fled by sea to Guangzhou, the last stronghold of the [Ming empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_dynasty "Ming dynasty"). On December 11, he declared himself the Shaowu Emperor, borrowing his imperial regalia from local theater troupes.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985737-93) He led a successful offense against his cousin [Zhu Youlang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Youlang "Zhu Youlang") but was deposed and executed on January 20, 1647, when the Ming turncoat Li Chengdong ([李](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%9D%8E "wikt:李")[成](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%88%90 "wikt:成")[棟](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%A3%9F "wikt:棟")) sacked the city on behalf of the [Qing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_dynasty "Qing dynasty").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985738-94)

In May 1648, Li Chengdong rebelled against the Qing and declared his allegiance to the [Southern Ming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Ming "Southern Ming"), making Guangzhou a base for the Ming loyalist resurgence in southern China.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985764%E2%80%93767-95) On 24 November 1650, after a prolonged siege during the [Qing conquest of southern China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transition_from_Ming_to_Qing "Transition from Ming to Qing"), [Shang Kexi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shang_Kexi "Shang Kexi")'s forces captured Guangzhou and launched a large-scale massacre of Ming loyalists and civilians, killing up to 70,000 people.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWakeman1985767%E2%80%93768-96)

The Qing became somewhat more receptive to foreign trade after gaining control of [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Tungning "Kingdom of Tungning") in 1683.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerdue2009-97) The [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire") from [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Macau "Colonial Macau") and [Spaniards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire") from [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Philippines "Spanish Philippines") returned, as did private Muslim, [Armenian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians "Armenians"), and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_England "Kingdom of England") traders.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) From 1699 to 1714, the [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV's_East_India_Company "Louis XIV's East India Company") and [British East India Companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company "East India Company") sent a ship or two each year;[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) the [Austrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Empire "Austrian Empire")[Ostend General India Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostend_Company "Ostend Company") arrived in 1717,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEButel1997197-99) the [Dutch East India Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_India_Company "Dutch East India Company") in 1729,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-100) the [Danish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway-Denmark "Norway-Denmark")[Asiatic Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_Asiatic_Company "Danish Asiatic Company") in 1731, and the [Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sweden "Kingdom of Sweden")[East India Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_East_India_Company "Swedish East India Company") the next year.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) These were joined by the occasional [Prussian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Prussia "Kingdom of Prussia") or [Trieste Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trieste_Company "Trieste Company") vessel. The first independent American ship arrived in 1784, and the first [colonial Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Australia "Colonial Australia") one in 1788.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] By that time, Guangzhou was one of the world's greatest ports, organized under the [Canton System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_System "Canton System").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKjellberg197599-101) The main exports were [tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_tea "History of tea") and [porcelain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_porcelain "Chinese porcelain").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGunn2011[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidE10tnvapZt0CpgPA208_208]-98) As a meeting place of merchants from all over the world, Guangzhou became a major contributor to the rise of the modern global economy.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-102) Guangzhou is the site of the [Thirteen Factories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Factories "Thirteen Factories"), which were the only legal place to conduct foreign trade with China from 1757 to 1842.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-103):xviii

In the 19th century, most of the city's buildings were still only one or two stories. However, there were notable exceptions such as the [Flower Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower_Pagoda "Flower Pagoda") of the [Temple of the Six Banyan Trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_of_the_Six_Banyan_Trees "Temple of the Six Banyan Trees"), and the guard tower known as the [Five-Story Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhenhai_Tower_(Guangzhou) "Zhenhai Tower (Guangzhou)"). The subsequently urbanized northern hills were bare and covered with traditional graves. The brick city walls were about 6 miles (10 km) in circumference, 25 feet (8 m) high, and 20 feet (6 m) wide. Its eight main gates and two water gates all held guards during the day and were closed at night. The wall rose to incorporate a hill on its northern side and was surrounded on the other three by a moat which, along with the canals, functioned as the city's sewer, emptied daily by the river's tides. A partition wall with four gates divided the northern "old town" from the southern "new town" closer to the river; the suburb of [Xiguan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiguan "Xiguan") (Saikwan; "West Gate") stretched beyond and the boats of fishers, traders, and [Tanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanka_people "Tanka people") ("boat people") almost entirely concealed the riverbank for about 4 miles (6 km). It was common for homes to have a storefront facing the street and to treat their [courtyards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_courtyard_house "Chinese courtyard house") as a kind of warehouse.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''EB''187837-42) The city was part of a network of signal towers so effective that messages could be relayed to [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing")—about 1,200 miles (1,931 km) away—in less than 24 hours.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKjellberg197595-104)
