The Canton System was maintained until the outbreak of the [First Opium War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Opium_War "First Opium War") in 1839. Following a series of battles in the [Pearl River Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River_Delta "Pearl River Delta"), the British [captured Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Canton_(March_1841) "Battle of Canton (March 1841)") on March 18, 1841.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''Bulletins_&c.''1841357-105) The [Second Battle of Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Canton_(May_1841) "Battle of Canton (May 1841)") was fought two months later.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMacPherson1842312_&_315-106) Following the Qing's 1842 [treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Nanking "Treaty of Nanking") with [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland"), Guangzhou lost its privileged trade status as more and more [treaty ports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_port "Treaty port") were opened to more and more countries, usually including extraterritorial enclaves. Amid the decline of Qing prestige and the chaos of the [Red Turban Rebellion (1854–1856)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Turban_Rebellion_(1854%E2%80%931856) "Red Turban Rebellion (1854–1856)"), the [Punti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punti "Punti") and [Hakka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hakka "Hakka") waged [a series of clan wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punti-Hakka_Clan_Wars "Punti-Hakka Clan Wars") from 1855 to 1867 in which one million people died. The foreign trade facilities were destroyed by local Chinese in the [Arrow War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Opium_War "Second Opium War") (1856–1858). The international community relocated to the outskirts and most international trade moved through [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-107)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-108)

The concession for the [Guangzhou–Hankou railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou%E2%80%93Hankou_railway "Guangzhou–Hankou railway") was awarded to the [American China Development Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_China_Development_Company "American China Development Company") in 1898. It completed [its branch line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou%E2%80%93Sanshui_Railway "Guangzhou–Sanshui Railway") west to [Foshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foshan "Foshan") and [Sanshui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanshui "Sanshui") before being engulfed in a diplomatic crisis after a Belgian consortium bought a controlling interest and the Qing subsequently canceled its concession. [J. P. Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Morgan "J. P. Morgan") was awarded millions in damages[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-109) and the line to [Wuchang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuchang_District "Wuchang District") was not completed until 1936[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-110) and the completion of a unified [Beijing–Guangzhou railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing%E2%80%93Guangzhou_railway "Beijing–Guangzhou railway") waited until the completion of [Wuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan")'s [Yangtze River Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan_Yangtze_River_Bridge "Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge") in 1957.

### Modern China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Modern China")]

#### Revolutions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Revolutions")]

During the late Qing dynasty, Guangzhou was the site of revolutionary attempts such as the [Uprisings of 1895](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Guangzhou_Uprising "First Guangzhou Uprising") and [1911](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Guangzhou_Uprising#History "Second Guangzhou Uprising") that were the predecessors of the successful [1911 Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1911_Revolution "1911 Revolution"), which overthrew the Qing dynasty. The 72 revolutionaries whose bodies were found after the latter uprising are honored as the city's 72 [Martyrs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martyrdom_in_Chinese_culture "Martyrdom in Chinese culture") at the [Huanghuagang Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huanghuagang_Park?action=edit&redlink=1 "Huanghuagang Park (page does not exist)")[[zh](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%BB%84%E8%8A%B1%E5%B2%97%E5%85%AC%E5%9B%AD "zh:黄花岗公园")] (_Yellow Flower Mound Park_).

#### Republic of China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Republic of China")]

After the assassination of [Song Jiaoren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_Jiaoren "Song Jiaoren") and [Yuan Shikai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_Shikai "Yuan Shikai")'s attempts to remove the [Nationalist Party of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_Party_of_China "Nationalist Party of China") from power, the leader of Guangdong [Hu Hanmin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Hanmin "Hu Hanmin") joined the 1913 [Second Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Revolution_(China) "Second Revolution (China)") against him[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-111) but was forced to flee to [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan") with [Sun Yat-sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-sen "Sun Yat-sen") after its failure. The city came under national spotlight again in 1917, when Prime Minister [Duan Qirui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duan_Qirui "Duan Qirui")'s abrogation of the constitution triggered the [Constitutional Protection Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Protection_Movement "Constitutional Protection Movement"). [Sun Yat-sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-sen "Sun Yat-sen") came to head the [Guangzhou Military Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Protection_Junta "Constitutional Protection Junta") supported by the members of the dissolved parliament and the Southwestern warlords. The Guangzhou government fell apart as the warlords withdrew their support. Sun fled to [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_International_Settlement "Shanghai International Settlement") in November 1918 until the Guangdong warlord [Chen Jiongming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Jiongming "Chen Jiongming") restored him in October 1920 during the [Yuegui Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuegui_Wars "Yuegui Wars").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeck2007-112) On June 16, 1922, Sun was ousted in a coup and fled on the warship _[Yongfeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS\_Zhongshan "SS Zhongshan")_ after Chen sided with the [Zhili clique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhili_clique "Zhili clique")'s [Beijing government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beiyang_government "Beiyang government"). In the following months Sun mounted a counterattack into Guangdong by rallying supporters from Yunnan and Guangxi, and in January established [a government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_the_Republic_of_China_in_Guangzhou "Government of the Republic of China in Guangzhou") in the city for the third time.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

From 1923 to 1926, Sun Yat-sen and the [Kuomintang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuomintang "Kuomintang") (KMT) [used the city as a base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_and_Navy_Marshal_stronghold_of_the_Republic_of_China "Army and Navy Marshal stronghold of the Republic of China") to prosecute a renewed revolution in China by conquering the warlords in the north. Although Sun was previously dependent on opportunistic warlords who hosted him in the city, with the leadership of [Chiang Kai-shek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek "Chiang Kai-shek"), the KMT developed its own military power to serve its ambition. The Canton years saw the evolution of the KMT into a revolutionary movement with a strong military focus and ideological commitment, setting the tone of the KMT rule of China beyond 1927.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1924, the KMT made the momentous decision to ally with the Communist Party and the USSR. With Soviet help, KMT reorganized itself along the Leninist line and adopted a pro-labor and pro-peasant stance. The [KMT–CCP cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_United_Front "First United Front") was confirmed in the [1st National Congress of the KMT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_National_Congress_of_the_Kuomintang "1st National Congress of the Kuomintang") and the communists were instructed to join the KMT. The allied government set up the [Peasant Movement Training Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peasant_Movement_Training_Institute "Peasant Movement Training Institute") in the city, of which [Mao Zedong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong") was a director for one term. Sun and his military commander Chiang used [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USSR "USSR") funds and weapons to build an armed force staffed by communist commissars, training its cadres in the [Whampoa Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whampoa_Military_Academy "Whampoa Military Academy").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeck2007-112) In August, the fledgling army suppressed the [Canton Merchants' Corps Uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_Merchants'_Corps_Uprising "Canton Merchants' Corps Uprising"). The next year the anti-imperialist [May Thirtieth Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_Thirtieth_Movement "May Thirtieth Movement") swept the country, and the KMT government called for strikes in Canton and Hong Kong. The tensions of the massive strikes and protests led to the [Shakee Massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakee_Massacre "Shakee Massacre").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

After the death of Sun Yat-sen in 1925 the mood was changing in the party toward the communists. In August the left-wing KMT leader [Liao Zhongkai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_Zhongkai "Liao Zhongkai") was assassinated and the right-wing leader [Hu Hanmin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Hanmin "Hu Hanmin"), the suspected mastermind, was exiled to the Soviet Union, leaving the pro-communist [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei") in charge. Opposing communist encroachment, the right-wing [Western Hills Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hills_Group "Western Hills Group") vowed to expel the communists from the KMT. The [Canton Coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_Coup "Canton Coup") on March 20, 1926, saw Chiang solidify his control over the [Nationalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KMT "KMT") and [their army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Revolutionary_Army "National Revolutionary Army") against [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei"), the party's left wing, its [Communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") allies, and its [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USSR "USSR") advisors.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-113)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-AhXiang1998-114) By May, he had ended civilian control of the military[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-AhXiang1998-114) and begun his [Northern Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Expedition_(1926%E2%80%931927) "Northern Expedition (1926–1927)") against the [warlords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warlord_Era "Warlord Era") of the north. Its success led to the split of the KMT between Wuhan and Nanking and the purge of the communists in the [April 12 Incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_12_Incident "April 12 Incident"). Immediately afterwards Canton joined the purge under the auspice of [Li Jishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jishen "Li Jishen"), resulting in the arrest of communists and the suspension of left wing KMT apparatuses and labor groups. Later in 1927 when [Zhang Fakui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Fakui "Zhang Fakui"), a general supportive of the Wuhan faction, seized Canton and installed [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei")'s faction in the city, the communists saw an opening and launched the [Guangzhou Uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou_Uprising "Guangzhou Uprising"). Prominent communist military leaders [Ye Ting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_Ting "Ye Ting") and [Ye Jianying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_Jianying "Ye Jianying") led the failed defense of the city. Soon, control of the city reverted to [Li Jishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jishen "Li Jishen").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Li Jishen was deposed during a war between Chiang and the [New Guangxi clique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Guangxi_clique "New Guangxi clique"). By 1929, [Chen Jitang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Jitang "Chen Jitang") had established himself as the powerholder of Guangdong. In 1931 he threw his weight behind the anti-Chiang schism by hosting a separate Nationalist government in Guangzhou.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-115) The opposition to Chiang included KMT leaders like [Wang Jingwei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei"), [Sun Fo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Fo "Sun Fo") and others from diverse factions. The peace negotiations amid the armed standoff led to the [4th National Congress of Kuomintang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_National_Congress_of_Kuomintang "4th National Congress of Kuomintang") being held separately by three factions in Nanjing, Shanghai, and Canton. Resigning all his posts, Chiang pulled off a political compromise that reunited all factions. While the intraparty division was resolved, Chen kept his power until he was defeated by Chiang in 1936. During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the [Canton Operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_Operation "Canton Operation") subjected the city to [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan") occupation by the end of December 1938.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### People's Republic of China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guangzhou&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: People's Republic of China")]

Amid the closing months before total Communist victory, Guangzhou briefly served as the capital of the Republican government. Guangzhou was captured on October 14, 1949. Amid a massive exodus to [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Macau "Colonial Macau"), defeated Nationalist forces blew up the [Haizhu Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haizhu_Bridge "Haizhu Bridge") across the Pearl River in retreat. The Cultural Revolution had a large effect on the city, with many of its temples, churches and other monuments destroyed during this chaotic period.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") initiated building projects including new housing on the banks of the Pearl River to adjust the city's [boat people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanka_people "Tanka people") to life on land. Since the 1980s, the city's close proximity to [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and its ties to [overseas Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Chinese "Overseas Chinese") made it one of the first beneficiaries of China's [opening up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_up_policy "Opening up policy") under [Deng Xiaoping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping"). British pop duo [Wham!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wham! "Wham!") performed in the city in April 1985, their second China date of [the Big Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Big_Tour "The Big Tour") after Beijing, becoming the first Western pop act to perform in China.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-116) Beneficial tax reforms in the 1990s also helped the city's industrialization and economic development.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The municipality was expanded in the year 2000, with [Huadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huadu_District "Huadu District") and [Panyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panyu_District "Panyu District") joining the city as [urban districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_(China) "District (China)") and [Conghua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conghua "Conghua") and [Zengcheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zengcheng "Zengcheng") as more rural [counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(China) "County (China)"). The former districts of [Dongshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dongshan_District,_Guangzhou "Dongshan District, Guangzhou") and [Fangcun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fangcun_District "Fangcun District") were abolished in 2005, merged into [Yuexiu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuexiu_District "Yuexiu District") and [Liwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liwan_District "Liwan District") respectively. The city acquired [Nansha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nansha,_Guangzhou "Nansha, Guangzhou") and [Luogang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luogang_District "Luogang District"). The former was carved out of [Panyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panyu_District "Panyu District"), the latter from parts of [Baiyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baiyun_District,_Guangzhou "Baiyun District, Guangzhou"), [Tianhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianhe_District "Tianhe District"), [Zengcheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zengcheng "Zengcheng"), and an exclave within [Huangpu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_District,_Guangzhou "Huangpu District, Guangzhou"). The [National People's Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_People's_Congress "National People's Congress") approved a development plan for the [Pearl River Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River_Delta "Pearl River Delta") in January 2009; on March 19 of the same year, the Guangzhou and [Foshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foshan "Foshan") municipal governments agreed to establish a framework to merge the two cities.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-117) In 2014, [Luogang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luogang_District "Luogang District") merged into [Huangpu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_District,_Guangzhou "Huangpu District, Guangzhou") and both [Conghua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conghua_District "Conghua District") and [Zengcheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zengcheng_District "Zengcheng District") counties were upgraded to districts.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 16 June 2022, an [EF2 tornado struck the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornadoes_of_2022#June_16_(China) "Tornadoes of 2022"), causing major power outages and knocking out power to the city's subway lines.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-118)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-119)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangzhou#cite_note-120)

**Shanghai**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-12) is a provincial-level [direct-administered municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-administered_municipality "Direct-administered municipality") in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"). It has a population of 30,050,000 in the urban area as of 2026, thus making it [China's most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_China_by_population "List of cities in China by population") and more broadly [the fifth-largest city in the world by population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities "List of largest cities").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-13) The city is located on the southern [estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuary "Estuary") of the [Yangtze River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangtze_River "Yangtze River"), with the [Huangpu River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_River "Huangpu River") bisecting the city.

Shanghai is a global centre for finance, business, research, science and technology, manufacturing, transportation, [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tourist_attractions_in_Shanghai "List of tourist attractions in Shanghai"), and [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Shanghai "Culture of Shanghai"). The [Port of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Shanghai "Port of Shanghai") is the [world's busiest container port](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_busiest_container_port "World's busiest container port").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-14) As of 2022, the Greater Shanghai metropolitan area was estimated to produce a [gross metropolitan product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_metropolitan_product "Gross metropolitan product") ([nominal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP_(nominal) "GDP (nominal)")) of nearly 13 trillion [RMB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi") ($1.9 trillion).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-GDP2022-15)

Originally a [fishing village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing_village "Fishing village") and market town, Shanghai grew to global prominence in the 19th century due to domestic and foreign trade and its favorable port location. The city was one of five [treaty ports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_ports "Treaty ports") forced to open to trade with the [Europeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europeans "Europeans") after the [First Opium War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Opium_War "First Opium War"), with the [Shanghai International Settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_International_Settlement "Shanghai International Settlement") and [French Concession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_French_Concession "Shanghai French Concession") subsequently established. The city became a primary commercial and financial hub of [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") in the 1930s. During the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), it was the site of the [Battle of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Shanghai "Battle of Shanghai"), where it fell under Japanese rule. This was followed by the [Chinese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War "Chinese Civil War") with the [Communists taking over the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Campaign "Shanghai Campaign") and most of the mainland. During the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), trade was mostly limited to other socialist countries in the [Eastern Bloc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bloc "Eastern Bloc"), causing the city's global influence to decline.

The [reform and opening up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_and_opening_up "Reform and opening up") supported by [Deng Xiaoping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping") led to extensive redevelopment by the 1990s, particularly in the [Pudong New Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pudong_New_Area "Pudong New Area"), spurring the return of finance and foreign investment. The city has re-emerged as a hub for international trade and finance. It is the home of the [Shanghai Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Stock_Exchange "Shanghai Stock Exchange"), [the largest stock exchange in the Asia-Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_major_stock_exchanges "List of major stock exchanges") by [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization "Market capitalization") and the [Shanghai Free-Trade Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Free-Trade_Zone "Shanghai Free-Trade Zone"), the first [free-trade zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-trade_zone "Free-trade zone") in mainland China. It is ranked eighth globally on the [Global Financial Centres Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Financial_Centres_Index "Global Financial Centres Index"). Shanghai has been classified as an Alpha+ ([global first-tier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_city "Global city")) city by the [Globalization and World Cities Research Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network "Globalization and World Cities Research Network"). As of 2024, it is home to 13 companies of the [_Fortune_ Global 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_Global_500#Fortune_Global_500_of_2021 "Fortune Global 500")—the fourth-highest number of any city.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-FG-16) Shanghai is the world's second [largest city by scientific outputs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_scientific_output "List of cities by scientific output") and home to several [highly ranked universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_First-Class_Construction "Double First-Class Construction"), including [Fudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fudan_University "Fudan University"), [Shanghai Jiao Tong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Jiao_Tong_University "Shanghai Jiao Tong University") and [Tongji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongji_University "Tongji University").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-17) The [Shanghai Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Metro "Shanghai Metro"), first opened in 1993, is the [largest metro network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_metro_systems "List of metro systems") in the world by route length.

Shanghai has been described as a global finance and innovation hub, and it is one of the ten biggest economic hubs in the world. Featuring several architectural styles such as [Art Deco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") and [shikumen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shikumen "Shikumen"), the city contains the [Lujiazui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lujiazui "Lujiazui") skyline, and museums and historic buildings such as the [City God Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_God_Temple_of_Shanghai "City God Temple of Shanghai"), [Yu Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yu_Garden "Yu Garden"), the [China Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Pavilion "China Pavilion") and buildings along [the Bund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bund "The Bund"). Shanghai is known for its [cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_cuisine "Shanghai cuisine"), [local language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghainese "Shanghainese"), and cosmopolitan culture. It ranks sixth in the [list of cities with the most skyscrapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_with_the_most_skyscrapers "List of cities with the most skyscrapers").

The two [Chinese characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_character "Chinese character") in the city's name are [上](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E4%B8%8A "wikt:上") ([Pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"):_shàng_; [Wugniu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wugniu "Wugniu"):_zaon_, "upon") and [海](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%B5%B7 "wikt:海") (_hǎi_; _he_, "sea"), together meaning "On the Sea". The earliest occurrence of this name is the 11th-century [Song dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_dynasty "Song dynasty"), when there was a river confluence and a town with this name in the area. Others contend that the city is referenced in historical records dating back 2150 years, and that its ancient name, "Hu", suggests it was a fishing village. In 1280 it was renamed "Shanghai", which translates to "Above the Sea".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-18) The name's interpretation was disputed, but Chinese historians concluded that during the [Tang dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty "Tang dynasty"), the area of modern-day Shanghai was under sea level, so the land appeared to be "on the sea".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Danielson,_Eric_N._2004,_pp.8-9-19) The name was also used to refer to Shanghai county (上海县; 上海縣; _Shànghǎi Xiàn_; _zaon-he-yoe_), which today has been reorganised into [Minhang district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minhang_district "Minhang district").

Shanghai is officially abbreviated [沪](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%B2%AA "wikt:沪")[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-20) ([Traditional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_characters "Traditional characters"):[滬](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%BB%AC "wikt:滬"), _Hù_; _wu_) in [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"), a contraction of [沪渎](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%B2%AA%E6%B8%8E "wikt:沪渎")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-21) ([滬瀆](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%BB%AC%E7%80%86 "wikt:滬瀆"), _Hù Dú_; _wu-doq_, "[Fishing Weir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing_weir "Fishing weir") Ditch"), a 4th- or 5th-century[Jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jin_Dynasty_(265%E2%80%93420) "Jin Dynasty (265–420)") name for the mouth of [Suzhou Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzhou_Creek "Suzhou Creek") when it was the main conduit into the ocean.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Shenhu_Origin-22) This character appears on motor vehicle license plates issued in the municipality.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-23)

### Alternative names

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Alternative names")]

[申](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%94%B3 "wikt:申") (_Shēn_; _sén_) or [申](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%94%B3 "wikt:申")[城](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%9F%8E "wikt:城") (_Shēnchéng_; _sén-zen_, "Shen City") was an early name originating from [Lord Chunshen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Chunshen "Lord Chunshen"), a 3rd-century BC nobleman and prime minister of the [state of Chu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_(state) "Chu (state)"), whose [fief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") included modern Shanghai.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Shenhu_Origin-22)[华亭](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%8D%8E%E4%BA%AD "wikt:华亭") ([華亭](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E8%8F%AF%E4%BA%AD "wikt:華亭"), _Huátíng_; _gho-din_) was another early name for Shanghai. In AD 751, [Huating County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songjiang,_Shanghai "Songjiang, Shanghai") was established as the first [county-level administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(China) "County (China)") within modern-day Shanghai by [Zhao Juzhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Juzhen "Zhao Juzhen"), the governor of [Wu Commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_Commandery "Wu Commandery").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-24)

[魔](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E9%AD%94 "wikt:魔")[都](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E9%83%BD "wikt:都") (_Módū_; _mo-tú_, "monster/fiend/magical city"),[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-25) is a contemporary nickname for Shanghai.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-26) The name was first mentioned in _Mato_ (1924) by Japanese novelist [Shōfu Muramatsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sh%C5%8Dfu_Muramatsu "Shōfu Muramatsu").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-27) The city has various English nicknames including the "[New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") of China", in reference to its status as a cosmopolitan [megalopolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area "New York metropolitan area") and [financial hub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_hub "Financial hub"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-28) the "Pearl of the Orient", and the "Paris of the East".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-paris_of_the_east-29)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-30)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Shanghai "History of Shanghai")

For a chronological guide, see [Timeline of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Shanghai "Timeline of Shanghai").

### Antiquity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Antiquity")]

The western part of modern-day Shanghai was inhabited 6,000 years ago.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-31) During the [Spring and Autumn period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_and_Autumn_period "Spring and Autumn period") (approximately 771 to 476 BC), it belonged to the [Kingdom of Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_(state) "Wu (state)"), which was conquered by the [Kingdom of Yue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yue_(state) "Yue (state)"), which in turn was conquered by the Kingdom of Chu.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-ancient-32) During the [Warring States period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warring_States_period "Warring States period") (475 BC), Shanghai was part of the fief of [Lord Chunshen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Chunshen "Lord Chunshen") of Chu, one of the [Four Lords of the Warring States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Lords_of_the_Warring_States "Four Lords of the Warring States"). Local legends claim he ordered the excavation of the [Huangpu River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_River "Huangpu River"), an important river in the area. Its former or poetic name, the Chunshen River, gave Shanghai its nickname of "Shēn".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-ancient-32) Fishermen living in the Shanghai area then created a fish tool called the _hù_, which lent its name to the outlet of Suzhou Creek north of the [Old City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_City_of_Shanghai "Old City of Shanghai") and became a common nickname and [abbreviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_abbreviations "Chinese abbreviations") for the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-33)

### Imperial era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Imperial era")]

During the Tang and Song dynasties, Qinglong Town (青龙镇; 青龍鎮; [Wugniu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wugniu "Wugniu"):_chín-lon-tsen_) in modern [Qingpu District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qingpu_District "Qingpu District") was a major trading port. Established in 746, it developed into what was historically called a "giant town of the Southeast". The port experienced thriving trade with provinces along the [Yangtze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangtze "Yangtze") and the Chinese coast, as well as foreign countries such as Japan and [Silla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silla "Silla").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-kaogu-1) By the end of the [Song dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_dynasty "Song dynasty"), the centre of trading had moved downstream of the [Wusong River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wusong_River "Wusong River") to Shanghai.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-34) Its status was upgraded from a village to a market town in 1074; in 1172, a second sea wall was built to stabilize the ocean coastline, supplementing an earlier dike.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-35) From the [Yuan dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_dynasty "Yuan dynasty") in 1292 until Shanghai officially became a [municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipality "Municipality") in 1927, central Shanghai was administered as a county under [Songjiang Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songjiang_Prefecture "Songjiang Prefecture"), which had its seat in the present-day [Songjiang District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songjiang_District "Songjiang District").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-36)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Old_City_of_Shanghai_will_walls_and_seafront.jpg/250px-Old_City_of_Shanghai_will_walls_and_seafront.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Old_City_of_Shanghai_will_walls_and_seafront.jpg)

The [Old City of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_City_of_Shanghai "Old City of Shanghai") in the 17th century

Shanghai's first [city wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_wall "City wall") was built in 1554 to protect the town from raids by [Japanese pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wokou "Wokou"). It was 10 meters (33 ft) high and 5 kilometers (3.1 mi) in circumference. A [City God Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_God_Temple_of_Shanghai "City God Temple of Shanghai") was built in 1602 during the [Wanli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanli_Emperor "Wanli Emperor") reign. This honour was usually reserved for prefectural capitals and not normally given to a county seat like Shanghai. Scholars theorized that this reflected the town's economic importance.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Danielson,_Eric_N._2004,_p.10-37)

During the [Qing dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qing_dynasty "Qing dynasty"), two central government policy changes caused Shanghai to become one of the most important seaports in the [Yangtze Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangtze_Delta "Yangtze Delta") region. The first was in 1684, when the [Kangxi Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kangxi_Emperor "Kangxi Emperor") reversed the 1525 prohibition on oceangoing vessels. In 1732, the [Qianlong Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qianlong_Emperor "Qianlong Emperor") moved the customs office for [Jiangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangsu "Jiangsu") province (see [Customs House, Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customs_House,_Shanghai "Customs House, Shanghai")) from [Songjiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songjiang,_Shanghai "Songjiang, Shanghai") to Shanghai, and gave Shanghai exclusive control over customs collections for Jiangsu's foreign trade. Shanghai became the major trade port for the lower Yangtze region by 1735, despite being at the lowest administrative level in the political hierarchy.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-38)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Shanghai_1884.jpg/250px-Shanghai_1884.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shanghai_1884.jpg)

A map of Shanghai in 1884; Chinese area are in yellow, French in red/pink, British in blue, American in orange.

In the 19th century, international attention and recognition of its economic and trade potential at the [Yangtze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangtze "Yangtze") grew.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-39) British forces occupied the city during the [First Opium War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Opium_War "First Opium War").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-40) The war ended in 1842 with the [Treaty of Nanking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Nanking "Treaty of Nanking"), which opened Shanghai as one of the five [treaty ports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_ports "Treaty ports") for international trade.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-41) The [Treaty of the Bogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_the_Bogue "Treaty of the Bogue"), the [Treaty of Wanghia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Wanghia "Treaty of Wanghia"), and the [Treaty of Whampoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Whampoa "Treaty of Whampoa"), signed between 1843 and 1844, forced Chinese concession to European and American desires for visitation and trade in China. Britain, France, and the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") established a presence outside the walled city of Shanghai, which remained under the direct administration of the Chinese.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChronicles-42)

The Chinese-held Old City of Shanghai fell to rebels from the [Small Swords Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_Swords_Society "Small Swords Society") in 1853, but was regained by the Qing government in February 1855.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-43) In 1854, the [Shanghai Municipal Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Municipal_Council "Shanghai Municipal Council") was created to manage the foreign settlements. Between 1860 and 1862, the [Taiping rebels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiping_Rebellion "Taiping Rebellion")[twice attacked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Shanghai_(1861) "Battle of Shanghai (1861)") Shanghai and destroyed the city's eastern and southern suburbs, but failed to take the city.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-WellWilli-44) In 1863, the British settlement south of [Suzhou Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzhou_Creek "Suzhou Creek") (northern [Huangpu District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_District,_Shanghai "Huangpu District, Shanghai")) and the American settlement to the north (southern [Hongkou District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hongkou_District "Hongkou District")) joined to form the [Shanghai International Settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_International_Settlement "Shanghai International Settlement"). The French opted out of the Shanghai Municipal Council and maintained [its own concession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_French_Concession "Shanghai French Concession") at the city's south and southwest.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-45) The [First Sino-Japanese War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Sino-Japanese_War "First Sino-Japanese War") concluded with the 1895 [Treaty of Shimonoseki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Shimonoseki "Treaty of Shimonoseki"), which elevated Japan as another foreign power in Shanghai. Japan built the first factories in Shanghai, which were copied by other foreign powers. This international activity gave Shanghai the nickname "the Great [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens") of China".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-46)

### Republic era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Republic era")]

See also: [Shanghai Municipality (1927–1949)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Municipality_(1927%E2%80%931949) "Shanghai Municipality (1927–1949)")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Shanghai_Bund_seen_from_the_French_Concession.jpg/250px-Shanghai_Bund_seen_from_the_French_Concession.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shanghai_Bund_seen_from_the_French_Concession.jpg)

[The Bund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bund "The Bund") as seen from the [French Concession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_French_Concession "Shanghai French Concession") in the 1920s

In 1912, the Old City walls were dismantled as they blocked the city's expansion.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-47) In July 1921, the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") was founded in the [Shanghai French Concession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_French_Concession "Shanghai French Concession").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChronicles-42) On 30 May 1925, the [May Thirtieth Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_Thirtieth_Movement "May Thirtieth Movement") broke out when a worker in a Japanese-owned [cotton mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill") was shot and killed by a Japanese foreman.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Ku-48) Workers in the city then launched [general strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_strikes "General strikes") against [imperialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperialism "Imperialism"), which became nationwide protests that gave rise to [Chinese nationalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_nationalism "Chinese nationalism").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-49)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Longhua_Temple_in_Shanghai_%28Panorama%29.jpg/250px-Longhua_Temple_in_Shanghai_%28Panorama%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Longhua_Temple_in_Shanghai_(Panorama).jpg)

[Longhua Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longhua_Temple "Longhua Temple"), 1922

The golden age of Shanghai began with its elevation to [municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_(1927%E2%80%931949) "Shanghai (1927–1949)") after it was separated from [Jiangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangsu "Jiangsu") on 7 July 1927.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChronicles-42)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-GovHistory-50) This new Chinese municipality was 494.69 square kilometers (191.00 sq mi), and included the districts of [Baoshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baoshan_District,_Shanghai "Baoshan District, Shanghai"), [Yangpu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangpu_District "Yangpu District"), [Zhabei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhabei "Zhabei"), [Nanshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanshi_District,_Shanghai "Nanshi District, Shanghai"), and [Pudong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pudong "Pudong").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-GovHistory-50) Headed by a Chinese mayor and municipal council, the city's government implemented the [Greater Shanghai Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Shanghai_Plan "Greater Shanghai Plan") to create a new city centre in Jiangwan town of Yangpu district, outside the boundaries of the foreign concessions.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-51) The city became a commercial and financial hub of the [Asia-Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia-Pacific "Asia-Pacific") region in the 1930s.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-1930hub-52) During the ensuing decades, citizens of many countries immigrated to Shanghai; those who stayed for long periods⁠⁠ called themselves "[Shanghailanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghailander "Shanghailander")".[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-53) In the 1920s and 1930s, almost 20,000 [White Russians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Movement "White Movement") fled the newly established [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") to reside in Shanghai.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-54) These [Shanghai Russians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Russians "Shanghai Russians") constituted the second-largest foreign community. By 1932, Shanghai had become the world's fifth-largest city and home to 70,000 foreigners.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-55) In the 1930s, approximately 30,000 Jewish refugees from Europe arrived in the city.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-56)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Shanghai_of_Today%2C_Plate_23_-_Shanghai_Racecourse%2C_stands_and_administration.jpg/250px-Shanghai_of_Today%2C_Plate_23_-_Shanghai_Racecourse%2C_stands_and_administration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shanghai_of_Today,_Plate_23_-_Shanghai_Racecourse,_stands_and_administration.jpg)

Shanghai Racecourse, stands and administration, 1927

#### Japanese invasion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Japanese invasion")]

Main articles: [Battle of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Shanghai "Battle of Shanghai") and [Shanghai (1927–1949)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_(1927%E2%80%931949) "Shanghai (1927–1949)")

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Shanghai1937city_zhabei_fire.jpg/250px-Shanghai1937city_zhabei_fire.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shanghai1937city_zhabei_fire.jpg)

[Zhabei District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhabei_District "Zhabei District") on fire, 1937

On [28 January 1932](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_28_incident "January 28 incident"), Japanese military forces invaded Shanghai. More than 10,000 shops and hundreds of factories and public buildings[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-57) were destroyed, leaving Zhabei district ruined. About 18,000 civilians were either killed, injured, or declared missing.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChronicles-42) A ceasefire was brokered on 5 May.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-58) In 1937, the [Battle of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Shanghai "Battle of Shanghai") resulted in the occupation of the Chinese-administered parts of Shanghai outside of the International Settlement and the French Concession. People who stayed in the occupied city experienced hunger, oppression, or death.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-59) The foreign concessions were occupied by the Japanese on 8 December 1941 and remained occupied until Japan's surrender in 1945.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-60)

Many Jewish people arrived in Shanghai during the Japanese occupation period. A vice-consul for Japan in Lithuania, [Chiune Sugihara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiune_Sugihara "Chiune Sugihara"), issued thousands of visas to Jewish refugees escaping the [Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust "Holocaust"), and the Japanese government transferred many of them to Shanghai by November 1941. Other Jewish refugees travelled from Italy. The refugees from Europe were interned in the [Shanghai Ghetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Ghetto "Shanghai Ghetto") in Hongkou District after the Japanese [attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor"). After the [surrender of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrender_of_Japan "Surrender of Japan"), the Chinese Army liberated the Ghetto, and most of the Jews left over the next few years.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-61)

### People's Republic era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: People's Republic era")]

On 27 May 1949, the [People's Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army "People's Liberation Army") took control of Shanghai through the [Shanghai Campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Campaign "Shanghai Campaign"). Under the new People's Republic of China (PRC), Shanghai was one of only three municipalities not merged into neighboring provinces (the others being [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing") and [Tianjin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianjin "Tianjin")).[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-62) Most foreign firms moved their offices from Shanghai to [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong"), as part of a foreign [divestment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divestment "Divestment") due to the PRC's victory.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-63)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/1967-12_1967%E5%B9%B4_%E4%B8%8A%E6%B5%B7%E5%B8%82%E5%8D%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%B7%AF.jpg/250px-1967-12_1967%E5%B9%B4_%E4%B8%8A%E6%B5%B7%E5%B8%82%E5%8D%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%B7%AF.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1967-12_1967%E5%B9%B4_%E4%B8%8A%E6%B5%B7%E5%B8%82%E5%8D%97%E4%BA%AC%E8%B7%AF.jpg)

[Nanjing Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanjing_Road "Nanjing Road"), 1967, during the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution")

After the war, Shanghai's economy was restored. From 1949 to 1952, the city's agricultural and industrial output increased by 51.5% and 94.2%, respectively.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChronicles-42) As the industrial centre of China with the most skilled industrial workers, Shanghai became a centre for radical [leftism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-wing_politics "Left-wing politics") during the 1950s and 1960s.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-64) During the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution") (1966–1976), Shanghai's society was severely damaged. The majority of the workers in the Shanghai branch of the [People's Bank of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Bank_of_China "People's Bank of China") were [Red Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Guards "Red Guards"), and they formed a group called the Anti-Economy Liaison Headquarters within the branch.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Liu-2023-65):38 The Anti-Economy Liaison Headquarters dismantled economic organizations in Shanghai, investigated bank withdrawals, and disrupted regular bank service in the city.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Liu-2023-65):38 Despite the disruptions of the Cultural Revolution, Shanghai maintained economic production with a positive annual growth rate.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChronicles-42)

In 1990, [Deng Xiaoping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping") permitted Shanghai to initiate economic reforms, which reintroduced foreign capital to the city and developed the Pudong district, resulting in the birth of [Lujiazui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lujiazui "Lujiazui").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-66) That year, China's central government designated Shanghai as the "Dragon Head" of the [reform and opening up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_and_opening_up "Reform and opening up").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-67) In 2022, Shanghai experienced a large outbreak of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") cases and the [Chinese government locked down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Shanghai_COVID-19_outbreak "2022 Shanghai COVID-19 outbreak") the entire city on 5 April. This resulted in widespread food shortages across the city as food-supply chains were severely disrupted. These restrictions were lifted on 1 June.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-68)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Geography")]

Main article: [Geography of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Shanghai "Geography of Shanghai")

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Sprawling_Shanghai_2016-07-20.jpg/250px-Sprawling_Shanghai_2016-07-20.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sprawling_Shanghai_2016-07-20.jpg)

The urban area of Shanghai in 2016, along with [its major islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islands_of_Shanghai "Islands of Shanghai"). From northwest to southeast: [Chongming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chongming_Island "Chongming Island"), [Changxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changxing_Island_(Shanghai) "Changxing Island (Shanghai)"), [Hengsha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengsha_Island "Hengsha Island"), and the [Jiuduansha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiuduansha "Jiuduansha") shoals off Pudong. The Yangtze's natural [sediment discharge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sediment_transport "Sediment transport") can be seen.

Shanghai is located on the Yangtze [Estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuary "Estuary") of China's east coast, with the Yangtze River to the north, [Hangzhou Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Bay "Hangzhou Bay") to the south, and the [East China Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_China_Sea "East China Sea") to the east. The land is formed by the Yangtze's natural [deposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deposition_(geology) "Deposition (geology)") and modern [land reclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reclamation "Land reclamation") projects. It has [sandy soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loam "Loam"), and skyscrapers have to be built with deep concrete piles to avoid sinking into the soft ground.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChroniclesEnvir-69) The provincial-level [Municipality of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipality_of_Shanghai "Municipality of Shanghai") administers the estuary and many of its [surrounding islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islands_of_Shanghai "Islands of Shanghai"). It borders the provinces of [Zhejiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang "Zhejiang") to the south and [Jiangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangsu "Jiangsu") to the west and north.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-location-70) The municipality's northernmost point is on [Chongming Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chongming_Island "Chongming Island"), the second-largest [island in mainland China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_China "List of islands of China") after its expansion during the 20th century.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-71)

Shanghai is located on an [alluvial plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvial_plain "Alluvial plain") and the vast majority of its 6,340.5-square-kilometre (2,448.1-square-mile) land area is flat, with an average elevation of four metres (13 feet).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-topo-7) Tidal flat ecosystems exist around the estuary, but they have been reclaimed for agricultural purposes.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-72) The city's few hills, such as [She Shan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheshan_Hill "Sheshan Hill"), lie to the southwest; its highest point is the peak of [Dajinshan Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dajinshan_Island "Dajinshan Island") (103 metres or 338 feet) in Hangzhou Bay.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-topo-7) Shanghai has rivers, canals, streams, and lakes, and it is known for its rich water resources as part of the [Lake Tai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Tai "Lake Tai")[drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-waterresources-73)

Downtown Shanghai is bisected by the Huangpu River, a man-made [tributary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tributary "Tributary") of the Yangtze created by order of Lord Chunshen during the Warring States period.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-ancient-32) The historic centre of the city was located on the west bank of the Huangpu ([Puxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puxi "Puxi")), near the mouth of Suzhou Creek, connecting it with Lake Tai and the [Grand Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Canal_of_China "Grand Canal of China"). The central financial district, Lujiazui, was established on the east bank of the Huangpu (Pudong). Along Shanghai's eastern shore, the destruction of local [wetlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wetlands "Wetlands") due to the construction of [Pudong International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pudong_International_Airport "Pudong International Airport") has been partially offset by the protection and expansion of a nearby shoal, [Jiuduansha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiuduansha "Jiuduansha"), as a nature preserve.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-74)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Climate")]

Shanghai has a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") ([Köppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"): _Cfa_), with an average annual temperature of 17.5°C (63.5°F) for downtown areas and 16.2–17.2°C (61.2–63.0°F) for suburbs.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChroniclesEnvir-69) The city experiences four distinct seasons. Winters are temperate to cold and damp—northwesterly winds from [Siberia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberia "Siberia") can cause nighttime temperatures to drop below freezing. Each year, there are an average of 4.7 days with snowfall and 1.6 days with snow cover.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-SHChroniclesEnvir-69) Summers are hot and humid, and occasional downpours or [thunderstorms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorms "Thunderstorms") can be expected. On average, 21 days meet or exceed 35°C (95°F) annually.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-75) In summer and the beginning of autumn, the city is susceptible to [typhoons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon "Typhoon").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-wiphatelegraph-76)

The most pleasant seasons are generally spring, although changeable and often rainy, and autumn, which is usually sunny and dry. With monthly percent possible sunshine ranging from 28% in June to 46% in August, the city receives 1,754 hours of bright sunshine annually. According to China's seasonal division standard, from 2001 to 2025, Shanghai enters spring on 9 March, summer on 15 May, autumn on 5 October, and winter on 4 December. The average temperature for the three weeks from 19 July to 8 August is above 30°C (86.0°F). Extremes since 1951 have ranged from −10.1°C (13.8°F) on 31 January 1977 (unofficial record of −12.1°C (10.2°F) was set on 19 January 1893) to 40.9°C (105.6°F) on 21 July 2017[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-77) and 13 July 2022[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-78) at a [weather station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_station "Weather station") in [Xujiahui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xujiahui "Xujiahui"). It also has 32.1°C (89.8°F) as the highest ever daily minimum temperature at Xujiahui on 13 August 2010.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-79)

In 2025, the average temperature of Xujiahui was 19.43°C (67.0°F), which was 1.93°C higher than the average from 1991 to 2020. The average daily high temperature is 23.66°C (74.6°F), and the average daily low temperature is 16.44°C (61.6°F).

## Cityscape

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shanghai&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Cityscape")]

[The Bund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bund "The Bund"), located by the bank of the Huangpu River, is home to a row of early 20th-century architecture, ranging in style from the [neoclassical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassical_architecture "Neoclassical architecture")[HSBC Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSBC_Building,_Shanghai "HSBC Building, Shanghai") to the [Art Deco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") Sassoon House (now part of the [Peace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Hotel "Peace Hotel")).[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-art_deco-86) The area has been revitalized several times: the first was in 1986, with a new [promenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esplanade "Esplanade") by the Dutch architect Paulus Snoeren.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Potter-87) The second was before the [2010 Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expo_2010 "Expo 2010"), which includes restoration of the century-old [Waibaidu Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waibaidu_Bridge "Waibaidu Bridge") and reconfiguration of traffic flow.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-88)

Shanghai's construction boom during the 1920s and 1930s caused the city to have several Art Deco buildings.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-art_deco-86)[László Hudec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A1szl%C3%B3_Hudec "László Hudec"), a [Hungarian-Slovak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians_in_Slovakia "Hungarians in Slovakia") who lived in the city between 1918 and 1947,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-89) designed Art Deco buildings such as the [Park Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Hotel_Shanghai "Park Hotel Shanghai"), the [Grand Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Cinema_(Shanghai) "Grand Cinema (Shanghai)"), and the [Paramount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_(Shanghai) "Paramount (Shanghai)").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-90) Other prominent Art Deco-style architects are [Clement Palmer and Arthur Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P&T_Group "P&T Group"), who designed the Peace Hotel, the [Metropole Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropole_Hotel_(Shanghai)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Metropole Hotel (Shanghai) (page does not exist)"), and the [Broadway Mansions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_Mansions "Broadway Mansions");[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-91) and Austrian architect [C.H. Gonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._H._Gonda "C. H. Gonda"), who designed the [Capitol Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Theater_(Shanghai)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Capitol Theater (Shanghai) (page does not exist)").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Potter-87) One common architectural element is the [shikumen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shikumen "Shikumen") (石库门; 石庫門; [Wugniu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wugniu "Wugniu"): _zaq-khu-men_, "stone storage door") residence, typically two- or three-story gray brick houses with the front yard protected by a heavy wooden door in a stylistic stone arch.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-radical_quaintness-92) Each residence is connected and arranged in straight alleys known as [longtangs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longtang "Longtang") (弄堂; _lon-daon_).[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-radical_quaintness-92)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-93) Shanghai also has [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") neoclassical architecture or [Stalinist architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stalinist_architecture "Stalinist architecture"): most were erected between the founding of the [People's Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") in 1949 and the [Sino-Soviet Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Soviet_Split "Sino-Soviet Split") in the late 1960s when Soviet personnel came to China to aid in the development of a communist state. An example of Soviet neoclassical architecture in Shanghai is the [Shanghai Exhibition Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Exhibition_Center "Shanghai Exhibition Center").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-Lonely_Planet_-_undated_-_Lonely_Planet_review_for_Shanghai_Exhibition_Center-94)

Shanghai has 206 buildings 150m+ making it the seventh [city in the world with the most skyscrapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_with_the_most_skyscrapers "List of cities with the most skyscrapers").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-95) Some of [Shanghai's skyscrapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_skyscrapers_in_Shanghai "List of skyscrapers in Shanghai") include the [Jin Mao Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jin_Mao_Tower "Jin Mao Tower"), the [Shanghai World Financial Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_World_Financial_Center "Shanghai World Financial Center"), and the [Shanghai Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Tower "Shanghai Tower"), which was completed in 2015 and is currently the tallest building in China and the [third tallest in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings "List of tallest buildings").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-96) The Oriental Pearl Tower, at 468 m (1,535 ft), is located nearby at the northern tip of Lujiazui.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-97) Many areas in the former foreign concessions are well-preserved.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-art_deco-86) Despite rampant redevelopment, the Old City retains traditional architecture and designs, such as the [Yu Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yu_Garden "Yu Garden"), an elaborate [Jiangnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangnan "Jiangnan") style garden.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-98)

**Shanghai**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-12) is a provincial-level [direct-administered municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-administered_municipality "Direct-administered municipality") in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"). It has a population of 30,050,000 in the urban area as of 2026, thus making it [China's most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_China_by_population "List of cities in China by population") and more broadly [the fifth-largest city in the world by population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities "List of largest cities").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-13) The city is located on the southern [estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuary "Estuary") of the [Yangtze River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangtze_River "Yangtze River"), with the [Huangpu River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huangpu_River "Huangpu River") bisecting the city.

Shanghai is a global centre for finance, business, research, science and technology, manufacturing, transportation, [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tourist_attractions_in_Shanghai "List of tourist attractions in Shanghai"), and [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Shanghai "Culture of Shanghai"). The [Port of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Shanghai "Port of Shanghai") is the [world's busiest container port](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_busiest_container_port "World's busiest container port").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-14) As of 2022, the Greater Shanghai metropolitan area was estimated to produce a [gross metropolitan product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_metropolitan_product "Gross metropolitan product") ([nominal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP_(nominal) "GDP (nominal)")) of nearly 13 trillion [RMB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi") ($1.9 trillion).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-GDP2022-15)

Originally a [fishing village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing_village "Fishing village") and market town, Shanghai grew to global prominence in the 19th century due to domestic and foreign trade and its favorable port location. The city was one of five [treaty ports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_ports "Treaty ports") forced to open to trade with the [Europeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europeans "Europeans") after the [First Opium War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Opium_War "First Opium War"), with the [Shanghai International Settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_International_Settlement "Shanghai International Settlement") and [French Concession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_French_Concession "Shanghai French Concession") subsequently established. The city became a primary commercial and financial hub of [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") in the 1930s. During the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), it was the site of the [Battle of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Shanghai "Battle of Shanghai"), where it fell under Japanese rule. This was followed by the [Chinese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War "Chinese Civil War") with the [Communists taking over the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Campaign "Shanghai Campaign") and most of the mainland. During the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), trade was mostly limited to other socialist countries in the [Eastern Bloc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bloc "Eastern Bloc"), causing the city's global influence to decline.

The [reform and opening up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_and_opening_up "Reform and opening up") supported by [Deng Xiaoping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping") led to extensive redevelopment by the 1990s, particularly in the [Pudong New Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pudong_New_Area "Pudong New Area"), spurring the return of finance and foreign investment. The city has re-emerged as a hub for international trade and finance. It is the home of the [Shanghai Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Stock_Exchange "Shanghai Stock Exchange"), [the largest stock exchange in the Asia-Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_major_stock_exchanges "List of major stock exchanges") by [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization "Market capitalization") and the [Shanghai Free-Trade Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Free-Trade_Zone "Shanghai Free-Trade Zone"), the first [free-trade zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-trade_zone "Free-trade zone") in mainland China. It is ranked eighth globally on the [Global Financial Centres Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Financial_Centres_Index "Global Financial Centres Index"). Shanghai has been classified as an Alpha+ ([global first-tier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_city "Global city")) city by the [Globalization and World Cities Research Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network "Globalization and World Cities Research Network"). As of 2024, it is home to 13 companies of the [_Fortune_ Global 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_Global_500#Fortune_Global_500_of_2021 "Fortune Global 500")—the fourth-highest number of any city.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-FG-16) Shanghai is the world's second [largest city by scientific outputs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_scientific_output "List of cities by scientific output") and home to several [highly ranked universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_First-Class_Construction "Double First-Class Construction"), including [Fudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fudan_University "Fudan University"), [Shanghai Jiao Tong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Jiao_Tong_University "Shanghai Jiao Tong University") and [Tongji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongji_University "Tongji University").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#cite_note-17) The [Shanghai Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Metro "Shanghai Metro"), first opened in 1993, is the [largest metro network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_metro_systems "List of metro systems") in the world by route length.

Shanghai has been described as a global finance and innovation hub, and it is one of the ten biggest economic hubs in the world. Featuring several architectural styles such as [Art Deco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") and [shikumen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shikumen "Shikumen"), the city contains the [Lujiazui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lujiazui "Lujiazui") skyline, and museums and historic buildings such as the [City God Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_God_Temple_of_Shanghai "City God Temple of Shanghai"), [Yu Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yu_Garden "Yu Garden"), the [China Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Pavilion "China Pavilion") and buildings along [the Bund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bund "The Bund"). Shanghai is known for its [cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_cuisine "Shanghai cuisine"), [local language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghainese "Shanghainese"), and cosmopolitan culture. It ranks sixth in the [list of cities with the most skyscrapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_with_the_most_skyscrapers "List of cities with the most skyscrapers").
